title: Why a Town Has Been on Fire for 60 Years

thumbnail.plane: an empty cracked asphalt road in a dead winter forest with thick white smoke rising from the cracks, overcast sky, eerie, wide view
thumbnail.zoom: extreme close-up of a deep crack in asphalt with white smoke pouring out and an orange glow deep inside, dramatic light

shots.vo: There is a road in Pennsylvania where smoke rises out of the ground. Not from a chimney. From the road itself.
shots.prompt: a cracked abandoned two-lane asphalt road with white smoke rising from long cracks, leafless trees on both sides, overcast, eerie

shots.vo: Under your feet, the earth is burning. It has been burning since nineteen sixty-two.
shots.prompt: a cross-section view of the ground under a road, glowing orange embers deep underground beneath layers of rock and soil, dramatic

shots.vo: The town that stood here had more than a thousand people. Today, only a handful are left.
shots.prompt: an empty small-town street with overgrown grass where houses used to be, only the old concrete sidewalks and steps remain, autumn

shots.vo: So why has nobody put the fire out? After more than sixty years?
shots.prompt: white smoke drifting through a dead forest at dusk, bare trees, orange light low on the horizon, haunting

shots.vo: Centralia, Pennsylvania. A small coal-mining town. Churches, bars, family homes, kids riding bikes.
shots.prompt: a small American coal-mining town main street in the early 1960s, brick shops, a church steeple, parked 1960s cars, sunny day

shots.vo: Beneath it ran one of the richest seams of hard coal in America, riddled with old mine tunnels.
shots.prompt: an old abandoned coal mine tunnel with wooden support beams and black coal walls, lit by a single lantern

shots.vo: Coal built this town. Nobody imagined it would also destroy it.
shots.prompt: coal miners with lamps on their helmets walking out of a mine entrance at dusk, 1950s, seen from behind

shots.vo: May, nineteen sixty-two. The town decides to clean up its rubbish dump before Memorial Day. The usual way. They set it on fire.
shots.prompt: a burning rubbish dump in a small open pit at the edge of a town, orange flames and smoke, 1960s, evening

shots.vo: But the dump sits in an old pit, next to an opening into the abandoned mines. And the fire finds it.
shots.prompt: a dark opening in the rock wall of an old pit, small flames creeping into the hole, smoke curling inside

shots.vo: Down there, the fire reaches the coal. And coal does not just burn. It smoulders, for years.
shots.prompt: deep underground, a seam of black coal glowing red and orange with embers, heat haze, no people

shots.vo: Crews try to dig it out. They flood the tunnels. They pump in mud and ash. Each time, the fire slips away along the coal.
shots.prompt: 1960s workers with bulldozers digging a deep trench in muddy ground, smoke rising from the earth behind them, overcast

shots.vo: Here is why it never works. The old tunnels and cracks keep feeding the fire fresh air. And the coal goes on for miles.
Years pass. The ground in town gets warm. In winter, snow melts in strange patches.
shots.prompt: a backyard in winter where snow has melted in an irregular patch on the ground with steam rising from it, a wooden fence, quiet

shots.vo: Basements fill with deadly gas. People start getting sick.
shots.prompt: a dim basement of an old house with a gas meter and a warning glow, a faint haze in the air, eerie, no people

shots.vo: Then, in nineteen eighty-one, a twelve-year-old boy is walking in a backyard when the ground opens under his feet.
shots.prompt: a backyard with a large fresh sinkhole in the grass, steam and smoke rising from the hole, a tree at its edge, overcast

shots.vo: He falls into a steaming hole, deep enough to kill him. He hangs on to a tree root, until his cousin pulls him out.
shots.prompt: close-up of a child's hand gripping an exposed tree root at the edge of a dark steaming hole, dramatic light

shots.vo: Now the whole country is watching. And the question becomes impossible to ignore: can this fire be stopped at all?
shots.prompt: 1980s television news crews and reporters standing in a small town street with smoke rising behind them

shots.vo: In nineteen eighty-three, a federal study put a price on it. Six hundred and sixty-three million dollars, with no guarantee it would even work.
Moving the people would cost far less. So in nineteen eighty-four, Congress set aside forty-two million dollars to buy the town and move it.
shots.prompt: a family loading furniture into a moving truck in front of a small house, 1980s, sad mood, backs to camera

shots.vo: House after house was bought, and torn down.
shots.prompt: a bulldozer demolishing a small two-story wooden house in a quiet town, dust in the air, 1980s

shots.vo: So the hidden why is brutal and simple. It was cheaper to erase a town than to put out a fire.
shots.prompt: an empty grid of overgrown streets in a forest clearing where a town used to be, aerial view, autumn colors

shots.vo: Centralia emptied. In two thousand two, the Postal Service even took away its ZIP code.
The main highway into town cracked open, and had to be closed and moved.
shots.prompt: a long abandoned highway with huge cracks across it and smoke rising from them, barriers closing the road, overcast

shots.vo: And the fire? By some estimates, there is enough coal down there to keep it burning for up to two hundred and fifty years.
shots.prompt: deep underground, an endless glowing seam of burning coal stretching into darkness, orange and red, epic

shots.vo: Today, only a few people still live there. They refused to leave, and the fire burns on beneath them.
shots.prompt: a lone old house standing at the end of an empty overgrown street, smoke drifting in the distance, autumn

shots.vo: A whole town, gone. Not because of a war, or a flood. Because of one rubbish fire, in the wrong place.
shots.prompt: a small fire burning in a pit at night with sparks rising into the dark sky, ominous

shots.vo: So if you ever drive through the hills of Pennsylvania and see smoke rising from the ground, now you know why.
shots.prompt: a car driving along a quiet forest road in Pennsylvania hills at dusk, thin smoke rising from the roadside

shots.vo: And that is the hidden why.
shots.prompt: a single wisp of white smoke rising from a crack in dark ground, close-up, quiet
